full_citation: Bajpai RK, Reuss M (1980). A mechanistic model for penicillin production. J Chem Technol Biotechnol 30(1):332-344.
process_and_scale: Penicillin fermentation; mechanistic kinetics study; scale not stated in abstract.
model_class: Mechanistic unstructured first-principles model (growth kinetics, substrate inhibition, oxygen limitation).
validation_setup: Model formulation study; no dataset validation reported in abstract.
key_findings: Foundational mechanistic model of penicillin production; the kinetic structure later simulators extend.
limitations: Abstract-level evidence only; full text pending; assumption set to be confirmed from full text.
relevance_to_framework: First-principles kernel and declared-assumption baseline for the hybrid digital twin.

full_citation: Menezes JC, Alves SS, Lemos JM, de Azevedo SF (1994). Mathematical modelling of industrial pilot-plant penicillin-G fed-batch fermentations. J Chem Technol Biotechnol 61(2):123-138.
process_and_scale: Industrial pilot-plant penicillin-G fed-batch; 1 m3 stirred tanks.
key_findings: Mechanistic model of industrial-media penicillin-G fed-batch; demonstrates that model assumptions and parameters need revision when moving between process settings.
relevance_to_framework: Scale-transfer caution evidence for twin fidelity claims.

full_citation: Zangirolami TC, Johansen CL, Nielsen J, Jorgensen SB (1997). Simulation of penicillin production in fed-batch cultivations using a morphologically structured model. Biotechnol Bioeng 56(6):593-604.
model_class: Morphologically structured mechanistic model with compartments and inhibition effects.
key_findings: Structured morphology model captures hyphal differentiation effects on penicillin production.
limitations: Abstract-level only (PubMed 927 chars); complexity-cost trade-off pending full text.
relevance_to_framework: Evidence for the mechanism-complexity trade-off in twin design.

full_citation: Birol G, Undey C, Cinar A (2002). A modular simulation package for fed-batch fermentation: penicillin production. Comput Chem Eng 26(11):1553-1565.
process_and_scale: Penicillin fed-batch fermentor; modular simulation software.
model_class: Unstructured mechanistic model extending Bajpai-Reuss with pH, temperature, aeration rate, agitation power, substrate feed flow and CO2 evolution terms.
measured_inputs: pH, temperature, aeration rate, agitation power, substrate feed flow rate.
control_method: None (simulator); monitoring and fault-diagnosis application demonstrated.
faults_delays_drift_considered: Monitoring and fault diagnosis use case (abstract-level).
validation_setup: Software package released for research and educational use.
key_findings: Modular penicillin simulator adding environmental control variables and a CO2 evolution term to the Bajpai-Reuss model; applied to monitoring and fault diagnosis.
relevance_to_framework: Direct simulator ancestor of IndPenSim; earliest monitoring and fault-diagnosis precedent in the corpus.

full_citation: Montague GA, Morris AJ, Wright AR, Aynsley M, Ward A (1985). Parameter adaptive control of the fed-batch penicillin fermentation. IFAC Proc Vol 18(17):69-74.
process_and_scale: Penicillin fed-batch; 20-L pilot plant real-time experiments plus simulation.
model_class: Mechanistic models (Bajpai-based extended with CO2 terms; a new mechanistic model compared).
predicted_estimated_states: On-line biomass estimate; mould growth trajectory.
control_method: Parameter adaptive Generalised Predictive Control (long-range receding horizon) tracking a biomass reference trajectory.
faults_delays_drift_considered: Parameter adaptation handles model mismatch; no explicit sensor-fault handling.
validation_setup: Real-time experiments on a 20-L pilot plant fermenter.
key_findings: Adaptive predictive control of penicillin using on-line biomass estimated from CO2 measurement, the Bajpai model and an extended Kalman filter; part of an industrial project on optimising control of large fed-batch fermenters.
limitations: 1985-era; single pilot scale; complimentary-access abstract only.
relevance_to_framework: Historical anchor that predictive penicillin control with state estimation is not new; baseline framing for RQ4.

full_citation: Goldrick S, Stefan A, Lovett D, Montague G, Lennox B (2015). The development of an industrial-scale fed-batch fermentation simulation. J Biotechnol 193:70-82.
process_and_scale: Industrial-scale 100,000 L penicillin fermentation; simulated and validated against industrial data.
measured_inputs: Full set of process inputs and outputs from historical batch records.
predicted_estimated_states: Full process state including growth, morphology, metabolic production and degeneration.
control_method: Simulator with control loops (details in B7).
faults_delays_drift_considered: Batch-to-batch variation and in-batch fluctuation modelled.
validation_setup: Validated against historical industrial batch records.
key_findings: Development of the industrial-scale fed-batch fermentation simulation that became the core of the IndPenSim benchmark.
access_status: metadata-verified + abstract-read (PubMed 25449107); green OA copy available

full_citation: Goldrick S, Duran-Villalobos CA, Jankauskas K, Lovett D, Farid SS, Lennox B (2019). Modern day monitoring and control challenges outlined on an industrial-scale benchmark fermentation process. Comput Chem Eng 130:106471.
process_and_scale: IndPenSim industrial-scale 100,000 L penicillin fermentation (Penicillium chrysogenum); 100-batch dataset of about 2.5 GB.
model_class: First-principles simulator plus PLS Raman soft sensor, PCA/MSPC monitoring, QbD/PAT demonstration and fault detection algorithm.
measured_inputs: Online at 12 min: dissolved oxygen, weight, pH, temperature, off-gas CO2 and O2. Off-line every 12 h plus 4 h delay: penicillin, biomass, PAA, nitrogen, viscosity. Raman spectra every 30 min (200-2400 cm-1).
predicted_estimated_states: Penicillin P, biomass X, PAA, nitrogen N, substrate S (no off-line measurement exists), viscosity.
control_method: PID loops for temperature and pH; recipe-driven or operator-dependent substrate feed Fs and PAA flow FPAA.
faults_delays_drift_considered: Agitator trip, aeration faults, substrate faults, sensor errors; inlet concentration disturbances; 4-h off-line assay delay.
validation_setup: QbD three-stage PAT demonstration; PLS calibration on Raman spectra vs off-line penicillin; PCA on-line and off-line monitoring; fault detection across yearly campaigns; five-campaign production metrics.
key_findings: Benchmark and 100-batch dataset released with Raman spectra; PLS on Raman predicts penicillin comparably to off-line assays; campaign metrics quantify operator-dependent versus recipe control (below-target batches 2, 8, 6, 2, 5 across five campaigns).
limitations: Simulated data, not plant measurements; classical methods only; no modern ML closed loop.
relevance_to_framework: Benchmark authority, dataset source, PAT/QbD framing and fault scenario catalogue for the gated empirical phase.

full_citation: Metcalfe B, Acosta-Pavas JC, Robles-Rodriguez CE, Georgakilas GK, Dalamagas T, Aceves-Lara CA, Daboussi F, Koehorst JJ, Corrales DC (2025). Towards a machine learning operations (MLOps) soft sensor for real-time predictions in industrial-scale fed-batch fermentation. Comput Chem Eng 194:108991.
model_class: LSTM soft sensor inside an MLOps lifecycle pipeline (development, deployment, maintenance, monitoring).
measured_inputs: IndPenSim process measurements (full feature enumeration pending full text).
predicted_estimated_states: Penicillin concentration; real-time prediction plus 8-hour forecast horizon.
faults_delays_drift_considered: Concept drift assessed on deviation batches 91-100; Population Stability Index threshold triggers an automatic retraining alert.
validation_setup: Proof of concept on IndPenSim; drift evidenced by soft sensor performance falling below the PSI threshold.
key_findings: End-to-end MLOps pipeline automates the soft sensor lifecycle; PSI-based drift detection with automated retraining trigger.
limitations: Simulated data; proof of concept; no closed-loop control; input feature list pending full text.
relevance_to_framework: Closest prior work on monitoring reliability and drift-driven model maintenance.

full_citation: Zheng J, Ma L, Wu Y, Ye L, Shen F (2022). Nonlinear dynamic soft sensor development with a supervised hybrid CNN-LSTM network for industrial processes. ACS Omega 7(19):16653-16664.
model_class: Supervised hybrid CNN-LSTM network; nonlinear dynamic soft sensor.
predicted_estimated_states: Quality variables (target enumeration pending full text).
key_findings: CNN-LSTM hybrid captures nonlinear dynamic behaviour for soft sensing.
access_status: metadata-verified + abstract-read (OpenAlex; PMC full text available)
relevance_to_framework: Architecture evidence for the soft-sensor comparison layer.

full_citation: Hermann L, Kremling A (2025). A hybrid soft sensor approach combining partial least-squares regression and an unscented Kalman filter for state estimation in bioprocesses. Bioengineering 12(6):654.
process_and_scale: L-phenylalanine bioprocess; transferable method, not penicillin.
model_class: Hybrid PLS regression plus unscented Kalman filter state estimator.
measured_inputs: Easily measured process variables (pending full text).
predicted_estimated_states: Bioprocess states via fusion of data-driven estimates and observer correction.
key_findings: Combining a PLS soft sensor with a UKF improves state estimation over either component alone.
limitations: Different organism and process; transferability must be argued, not assumed.
relevance_to_framework: Observer-based estimation pattern for the twin estimation layer.

full_citation: Shukla K, Nagpal S, Vyas A (2026). Opportunities of digital twin in controlling and monitoring microbial processes in food fermentation. Syst Microbiol Biomanuf 6(3):56.
model_class: Review of digital twin components and enablers (soft sensors, cloud platforms, PAT, ML/AI, IoT).
control_method: Adaptive control discussed at review level.
faults_delays_drift_considered: Biological variability and contamination prediction discussed.
key_findings: DT opportunities: real-time monitoring and control, adaptive control, contamination prediction, metabolite and by-product estimation, fermenter simulation. Limitations: biological variability, no standardized frameworks, no common data platforms. Bench-scale results dominate.
limitations: Adjacent food-fermentation scope; no penicillin-specific evidence; ahead-of-print record.
relevance_to_framework: Scope boundary control and recent digital-twin context; re-verify at submission.

full_citation: Page MJ, McKenzie JE, Bossuyt PM, Boutron I, Hoffmann TC, Mulrow CD, et al (2021). The PRISMA 2020 statement: an updated guideline for reporting systematic reviews. PLOS Med 18(3):e1003583.
key_findings: PRISMA 2020 reporting guideline for systematic reviews.
relevance_to_framework: Reporting standard for the search and screening log.

full_citation: Luo D, He M, Darko J, Ly Seymour F, Maturana F (2024). The golden batch-driven root cause analysis for anomalies in bioreactor fermentation process. Front Manuf Technol 4:1392038.
process_and_scale: IndPenSim penicillin benchmark; 100 batches (67 healthy, 33 below-target).
model_class: Golden-batch statistical profile (per-time-point mean and 3-sigma bounds from healthy batches 61-90), symmetric MAPE deviation, CPP contribution analysis.
measured_inputs: Operator-defined CQAs and CPPs; IndPenSim online and off-line variables.
predicted_estimated_states: CQA deviations (penicillin) and CPP contributions (pH, dissolved oxygen, base flow rate).
faults_delays_drift_considered: Out-of-trend and out-of-spec anomalies; batch-duration truncation for alignment; dataset 4-h off-line delay inherent; drift not addressed.
validation_setup: IndPenSim case studies on batches 92, 96 and 99; comparison against PCA-based methods.
key_findings: Golden batch built from many healthy batches rather than one manually picked batch. Batch 99 deviates 54.03% with onset near 100 h (pH and DO top contributors). Batch 92 deviates 24.05% with onset near 160 h (base flow rate and DO). Healthy batch 96 still shows 11.52% deviation (pH, base flow rate). Fewer false positives and false negatives than PCA.
limitations: Offline post-hoc method; no streaming; truncation-based alignment; no control linkage.
relevance_to_framework: Monitoring and RCA method to extend to streaming; source of batch health labels.

full_citation: Rashedi M, Khodabandehlou H, Demers M, Wang T, Garvin C (2022). Model predictive controller design for bioprocesses based on machine learning algorithms. IFAC-PapersOnLine 55(7):45-50.
process_and_scale: Fed-batch mammalian cell culture (Amgen); 35 batches of 12 days; daily sampling.
model_class: Hybrid model: glucose mass balance plus linear regression or two-layer neural network; linear MPC.
measured_inputs: pH, dissolved oxygen, temperature, feed (sparse bolus); glucose GLC.
predicted_estimated_states: VCD, TCD, viability, glucose, lactate, glutamine, glutamate, ammonium, sodium, potassium, osmolality.
control_method: Linear MPC optimizing daily feed to maximize viable cell density with metabolite constraints.
faults_delays_drift_considered: Sparse non-uniform bolus feed data problem addressed via mass balance; no fault handling.
validation_setup: 35 historical batches for model identification; real bioreactor experiment for controller validation.
key_findings: Linear regression beat the neural network on normalized RMSE; the mass-balance hybrid handles feed sparsity; MPC achieved over 2% improvement in final protein production versus the historical average.
limitations: Single manipulated input (feed); daily control timescale; small dataset; mammalian cell culture, not microbial.
relevance_to_framework: Hybrid modelling and MPC evidence; simplicity-wins caution for the control layer.

full_citation: Kwon HJ, Shiu JH, Yamakawa CK, Rivera EC (2024). Enhancing fermentation process monitoring through data-driven modeling and synthetic time series generation. Bioengineering 11(8):803.
process_and_scale: Very-high-gravity ethanol fermentation from sugarcane; 11 cycles; 3-L Bioflo 115 with 2-L working volume; intensified cell-reuse process.
model_class: Convolutional VAE for synthetic time-series generation plus feedforward neural network regression soft sensor.
measured_inputs: Electrical capacitance, redox potential, pH, temperature.
faults_delays_drift_considered: Noisy probes, sensor malfunction, missing and corrupt data, sparse dataset.
validation_setup: Original versus augmented training (Augmented10, Augmented100); 100-iteration resampled testing; R-squared and RMSE.
key_findings: VAE augmentation improved soft sensor R-squared by 34% and reduced variability by 82%; process context includes cascaded temperature setpoints and late-stage micro-aeration.
limitations: Lab scale; ethanol only; no closed loop; augmentation quality depends on VAE fidelity.
relevance_to_framework: Small-data augmentation recipe portable to penicillin soft sensors.

full_citation: Zhu X, Rehman KU, Wang B, Shahzad M (2020). Modern soft-sensing modeling methods for fermentation processes. Sensors 20(6):1771.
process_and_scale: Fermentation processes; review spanning marine alkaline protease, lysozyme, penicillin and L-lysine fermentations.
model_class: Review taxonomy: mechanism-based, data-driven (SVM, LS-SVM, neural networks, deep learning, fuzzy logic, probabilistic latent variable models) and hybrid; optimizers PSO, ant colony, artificial bee colony, cuckoo search, genetic algorithm.
predicted_estimated_states: Cell concentration, substrate concentration, product concentration (hard-to-measure targets).
faults_delays_drift_considered: Time-varying, nonlinear and strongly coupled process nature discussed; drift not systematically covered.
validation_setup: Review of more than 70 publications; evidence mostly simulation-based.
key_findings: Soft sensing is the core route to real-time estimation of unmeasurable variables; most work remains simulation-only with few industrial deployments.
relevance_to_framework: Method taxonomy for the soft-sensor comparison table; gap evidence on industrial deployment.

full_citation: Mondal PP, Galodha A, Verma VK, Singh V, Show PL, Awasthi MK, Lall B, Anees S, Pollmann K, Jain R (2023). Review on machine learning-based bioprocess optimization, monitoring, and control systems. Bioresour Technol 370:128523.
process_and_scale: Bioprocessing across biopharmaceuticals, biofuels and wastewater; review.
model_class: Review of ANN, GA, RSM, SVM, PLS, CNN, LSTM, DNN and hybrid models; cyber-physical and IoT integration.
measured_inputs: Process and sensor data across unit operations (review-level).
predicted_estimated_states: Critical quality attributes and critical process parameters.
control_method: Monitoring, optimization and predictive control discussed.
faults_delays_drift_considered: Time-delayed and scale-dependent responses, process drifts and disturbances listed as challenges.
validation_setup: Review; notes limited real-time application due to data scarcity, sensor lag and storage scalability.
key_findings: PLS and ANN dominate biopharmaceutical applications; hybrid models recommended; data management and cyber-integrated sensors are prerequisites; ML can classify batch quality and forecast process behavior.
limitations: Review; breadth over depth; no penicillin-specific benchmark.
relevance_to_framework: Landscape framing and gap evidence on deployment and data infrastructure.

full_citation: Gil JD, Del Rio Chanona EA, Guzman JL, Berenguel M (2026). Reinforcement learning meets bioprocess control through behavior cloning: Real-world deployment in an industrial photobioreactor. Eng Appl Artif Intell 164:113326.
process_and_scale: Open raceway photobioreactor; microalgae; industrial scale.
model_class: Offline DDPG reinforcement learning with behavior cloning from PID trajectories; recurrent actor-critic networks; POMDP formulation; nightly online fine-tuning.
measured_inputs: Observations: temperature, irradiance, dissolved oxygen, dilution flow, air flow, CO2 injection rate, time-of-day features, actuator values, pH error and clipped integral of error.
predicted_estimated_states: pH (controlled variable); hidden biomass inferred from observations.
control_method: RL policy manipulates CO2 injection rate (0-10 L/min) to regulate pH; logarithmic reward; anti-windup clipping of the error integral.
faults_delays_drift_considered: Partial observability, environmental disturbances and day-night cycle; nightly fine-tuning adapts to evolving dynamics.
validation_setup: Simulation studies plus 8-day real facility deployment.
key_findings: IAE reduced 8% versus PID, 6% versus MPC and 5% versus standard off-policy RL; control effort reduced 54% versus PID, 11% versus MPC and 7% versus off-policy RL; first industrial RL validation in a bioprocess.
limitations: Regulation task only (pH); not fed-batch fermentation; continual fine-tuning destabilization risk managed by epoch limits.
relevance_to_framework: Control-layer evidence and the offline-to-online adaptation pattern for the architecture adaptive layer.
